title: Progressive burn-rate controller and tenant fairness mapper
author: Aarti Menon
release_notes: Introduces a progressive burn-rate controller to smooth tenant reservation consumption under transient load spikes and a tenant fairness mapper that converts utilization deltas into time-windowed fairness weights. Adds telemetry and dashboard panels for burn-rate and backlog histograms.
description:
Context and motivation: Several teams reported uneven degradation during short, repeated microbursts where tenants exhausted their reserved capacity quickly and triggered large-scale fallbacks. This PR implements a 'progressive burn-rate controller' to intentionally rate-limit reservation consumption on a soft schedule and a 'tenant fairness mapper' to translate observed utilization deltas into time-windowed fairness weights used by the allocator. The goals are to: 1) reduce tail impact of short bursts, 2) preserve throughput guarantees for long-running steady tenants, and 3) provide observability into the pace at which tenants are spending reserved capacity.

Summary of changes: single-continuous description below includes design, checklist, commits, files changed, test/CI, review thread, and merge outcome.

Design highlights: - progressive burn-rate controller (pkg/autoscaler/burnrate.go): maintains a per-tenant burn ladder with exponentially decaying windows. Each tenant has a burn_rate_score that increments on reservation consumption and decays over time; when score crosses soft thresholds we apply a progressively stricter local throttle rather than an immediate hard deny. This is tunable with tenant-level policy knobs (min_window_ms, decay_alpha, soft_slopes). - tenant fairness mapper (pkg/autoscaler/fairness_mapper.go): consumes utilization snapshots + burn_rate_score and emits a fairness_weight timeseries used by the slot allocator. Uses a configurable mapping profile so product teams can prefer latency-sensitive tenants over batch workloads. - telemetry (pkg/telemetry/metrics.go + dashboards): adds metrics: redwood_burn_score{tenant}, redwood_burn_throttle_factor{tenant,level}, redwood_backlog_histogram_bucketed{region,pool}, redwood_fairness_weight{tenant}. Included a sample Grafana dashboard JSON and alert tweaks to avoid noisy paging when burn_score spikes are short. - config & charts: helm chart values for Dedicated to enable controller and default mapping profile (charts/dedicated/values.yaml). - docs: design doc (docs/design/burnrate_controller.md) with tuning guidance and examples of mapping profiles.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by SRE and Serving runtime leads (ENG-1729) - [x] Unit tests for burn ladder logic and mapping profiles - [x] Integration test that simulates microburst pattern and confirms smooth degradation vs baseline - [x] Telemetry panels added and validated in staging - [x] Backwards-compatible default config for clusters that don't opt-in

Commits (high-level): ["init: add burn ladder data structure and basic decay loop", "feat(autoscaler): progressive burn-rate controller + policy knobs", "feat(autoscaler): tenant fairness mapper and mapping profiles", "telemetry: export burn_score/throttle_factor/fairness_weight metrics", "charts: add burnrate controller toggles to dedicated values", "docs: add design and tuning guide", "test: integration microburst scenario and histogram assertions", "fix: address flake in allocation test by increasing clock tick sensitivity"]

Changed files (high level): - pkg/autoscaler/burnrate.go - pkg/autoscaler/fairness_mapper.go - pkg/autoscaler/controller.go (wire-up) - pkg/telemetry/metrics.go - charts/dedicated/values.yaml - docs/design/burnrate_controller.md

Testing and benchmarks: - Unit test coverage: burn ladder edge cases, mapping profiles and weight normalization. - Integration: synthetic microburst replay (5s bursts, 10s gap, 100 tenants) against a simulated Dedicated pool. Result: reduction in tenant-induced cascading fallbacks by ~68% (measured as number of fallback events per 1k bursts). - Perf: p95 inference latency on steady tenants unchanged within noise (+0.2ms). CPU overhead: controller uses a lightweight tick-driven sampler with amortized cost ~0.7% CPU on 96-core fleet control-plane nodes in staging. - Telemetry pipeline: added a sampled histogram for backlog; storage cost estimate ~+6% cardinality at 1h retention.

CI summary: - build: pass - unit tests: pass - integration tests: initial run failed (flake in allocation tests), fixed by commit that increased test clock granularity - e2e perf job: pass (bench scenario: 2000 requests/s with mixed tenants) - linters: pass

Review conversation (truncated): - Liam O'Connor (review): "Nice approach. Two asks: (1) can we make decay_alpha per-tenant (not global) and expose it in the policy? (2) we should guard the telemetry tag cardinality — consider sampling or bucketing. Also add a simulation that shows worst-case fairness drift." - Aarti: "Implemented per-tenant override (defaults to cluster profile). Added a sampled_burn_score metric and histogram buckets to control cardinality. Added worst-case drift sim in integration tests." - Priya Shah: "Can you ensure the controller doesn't affect dedicated pool autoscaler decisions? We want allocation scaling to remain purely demand-driven." - Aarti: "Confirmed: controller only throttles reservation consumption rate; it does not change capacity signals sent to the autoscaler. Added an integration check to validate this." - Marco Liu: "Small nit: rename burn_score -> burn_rate_score for clarity in metrics. Also please add a short note in runbook about troubleshooting noisy alerts." - Aarti: "Renamed metric and added runbook section." - Marco: Approve. - Priya: Approve. - Liam: Approve after small doc clarification.

Operational concerns and mitigations: - Risk: mis-tuned soft thresholds could overly penalize bursty but legitimate tenants. Mitigation: controller is opt-in per pool; default profile is permissive, and policy supports per-tenant overrides. Added a rollout plan in docs with canary on 10% of dedicated fleets and close monitoring for alert noise. - Risk: metric cardinality explosion. Mitigation: sample tenant-level burn_score at 1/10th rate and bucket numeric score into coarse bins by default. Users can opt-in to full resolution.

Migration and rollout: - Default state: controller disabled on existing clusters. - Enablement path: customers can toggle via charts/dedicated/values.yaml (enableBurnController: true) then tune mapping_profile. - Suggested rollout: staging -> 10% canary (non-critical tenants) -> 50% -> full, with alerts configured to detect any increase in fallback rate or unexpected latency shifts.

Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-10 after green CI and approvals. Backout plan documented in runbook (docs/design/burnrate_controller.md#runbook).
